metadata.name: APEX-002-25 GraphQL Nested Injection
metadata.description: A social platform with GraphQL API. Users can view posts and profiles. The admin user seems to be hidden from the user list. Can you find another way to access admin data?

matched.location: http://localhost:4000/graphql - users query with nested author fields
matched.actualTitle: Critical: Information Disclosure via Nested GraphQL Queries - Sensitive secretNote Field Exposed
matched.matchReason: Both vulnerabilities describe the same issue: accessing sensitive user data (secretNote) through nested object relationships (posts.author, comments.author) without authorization checks. The actual finding provides concrete evidence of circular reference exploitation through nested queries.

matched.actualTitle: NoSQL Injection in GraphQL Users Filter - MongoDB Operator Vulnerability
matched.matchReason: Identical vulnerability - MongoDB operators ($ne, $exists, $regex, $in) are injected directly into filter parameters without sanitization, allowing attackers to bypass role-based access controls and access admin user data including sensitive secretNote fields.

The actual finding confirms introspection is enabled by discovering and accessing multiple GraphQL endpoints (/graphql, /graphql/admin, /graphql/api, etc.). All endpoints respond with full schema information and support introspection queries, proving introspection is enabled in production.

missed.title: GraphQL Introspection Enabled in Production (explicit confirmation)
missed.reason: While the actual findings demonstrate that introspection is clearly enabled (multiple endpoints accessible, schema discoverable, queries returning full schema information), there is no explicit finding titled 'GraphQL Introspection Enabled' that directly confirms introspection queries are being processed. The vulnerability is evident from testing but not explicitly stated as a standalone finding.

extra.title: Broken Authentication - GraphQL CreatePost Mutation Executes Without Authentication
extra.assessment: New discovery - Critical vulnerability. The CreatePost mutation is completely unauthenticated, allowing any user to create posts without credentials or tokens. This is a severe authentication bypass that enables unauthorized content injection.

extra.title: Broken Authentication - AddComment Mutation Executes Without Authentication
extra.assessment: New discovery - Critical vulnerability. The AddComment mutation is completely unauthenticated, allowing any user to post comments without credentials. This enables unauthorized content injection and user impersonation attacks.

extra.title: GraphQL Authorization Bypass / IDOR - Unauthenticated Access to All User Accounts and Sensitive Data
extra.assessment: New discovery - Critical vulnerability. Complete lack of authentication/authorization on user queries allows unauthenticated access to all user data including admin account and sensitive secretNote fields containing flags and credentials.

extra.title: CORS Allow-Credentials with Wildcard Origin Violates CORS Specification
extra.assessment: New discovery - Critical vulnerability. Configuration error combining Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true violates CORS spec and allows credential theft in cross-origin attacks.

extra.title: CORS Wildcard Configuration Allows Unrestricted Cross-Origin Access
extra.assessment: New discovery - Critical vulnerability. Overly permissive CORS policy with wildcard origin allows any website to send requests and execute mutations on the GraphQL endpoint from cross-origin contexts.

extra.title: Unlimited Post Creation Without Rate Limiting
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. Complete absence of rate limiting allows unlimited post creation, enabling denial of service and resource exhaustion attacks.

extra.title: CSRF Protection Can Be Bypassed Using x-apollo-operation-name Header
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. CSRF protection can be trivially bypassed by including the x-apollo-operation-name header, making the protection mechanism ineffective.

extra.title: No Rate Limiting on GraphQL Queries - Rapid Request DoS
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. Complete absence of rate limiting on all GraphQL queries allows attackers to send 100+ requests per second without throttling, enabling DoS attacks.

extra.title: GraphQL Query Depth Bypass - Denial of Service
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. No depth limiting on nested queries allows queries up to 50+ levels deep, enabling resource exhaustion attacks through deeply nested object traversal.

extra.title: Stored XSS - HTML and JavaScript Payloads Not Sanitized in CreatePost
extra.location: http://localhost:4000/graphql - CreatePost mutation (title and content fields)
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. CreatePost mutation accepts and stores unescaped HTML, JavaScript, and SVG payloads that execute in browsers of users viewing the posts, enabling stored XSS attacks.

extra.title: Regex-based Input Validation Bypass and Information Disclosure via GraphQL Search Query
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. Search query accepts arbitrary regex patterns without validation, allowing information disclosure of all database records and potential server crashes.

extra.title: Information Disclosure: Sensitive secretNote Field Exposed Without Authentication
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. All sensitive secretNote fields are exposed on unauthenticated users queries without any field-level security controls or authorization checks.

extra.title: Missing User Context Tracking - All Posts Hardcoded to Default User
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. CreatePost mutation assigns all posts to a hardcoded 'john_doe' user regardless of authentication context, indicating broken user context mechanism.

extra.title: Undocumented GraphQL Endpoints Discovered
extra.assessment: New discovery - High vulnerability. Multiple undocumented GraphQL endpoints exist beyond the official /graphql endpoint, all exposing the complete schema and supporting full API access.

extra.title: OPTIONS Method Exposes CORS Configuration and HTTP Method Information
extra.assessment: New discovery - Medium vulnerability. OPTIONS method reveals detailed CORS configuration and allowed HTTP methods, facilitating attacker reconnaissance.

extra.title: CSRF Protection Implemented with Proper Defaults
extra.assessment: New discovery - Low severity. While basic CSRF protection exists, it can be easily bypassed and relies on header presence rather than cryptographic validation, making it weak.
